accepted.s:
With reference to the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme, consider the following statements:
1. It was revamped as DILRMP from 1 April 2016.
2. It was converted into a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding.
3. The Department of Land Resources under the Ministry of Rural Development is associated with its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. DILRMP was revamped from 1 April 2016, became fully centrally funded, and is handled by the Department of Land Resources under the Ministry of Rural Development.
accepted.tq: Check the date, funding pattern and administrative department together before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: The tenure of DILRMP was extended up to which period, along with which two new components?
o: 2025-26; consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts
2030-31; ULPIN generation and drone mapping
2024-25; GST integration and urban mapping
2026-27; biometric registration and agricultural census
accepted.x: The programme was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26. Consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts were added as new components.
accepted.tq: Pair the extension period with the two newly added components.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a core component of DILRMP?
o: Modern record rooms at tehsil level
Computerised registration and core GIS
Digitisation of cadastral maps and FMBs
Universal digitisation of agricultural subsidy beneficiary accounts
accepted.x: Modern record rooms, survey or resurvey, data entry, cadastral-map digitisation, State data centres, computerised registration and core GIS are DILRMP components. Universal digitisation of agricultural subsidy beneficiary accounts is not listed as a core component.
accepted.tq: Find the option that belongs to a neighbouring policy area rather than land-record modernisation.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the mandatory gender-related provision in the Record of Rights under DILRMP?
o: A separate gender-based land tax is recorded in the Record of Rights.
Only the gender of the registering officer is entered.
A mandatory gender column is included in the Record of Rights.
Gender details are excluded from digitised land records.
accepted.x: DILRMP provides for a mandatory gender column in the Record of Rights.
accepted.tq: Look for the precise record-level provision rather than an administrative or taxation alternative.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the phases of DILRMP 3.0.

List-I (Phase)
a. Phase 1
b. Phase 2
c. Phase 3

List-II (Focus)
i. GIS-based Land Stack for rural, semi-urban and urban parcels
ii. ULPIN, NGDRS, multilingual records and e-Court integration
iii. Digitisation, resurvey, cadastral maps and registration-mutation link

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: a-iii, b-ii, c-i
a-ii, b-iii, c-i
a-iii, b-i, c-ii
a-i, b-ii, c-iii
accepted.x: Phase 1 (2008-16) focused on digitisation, resurvey, maps and registration-mutation linkage; Phase 2 (2016-26) added ULPIN, NGDRS and related integration; Phase 3 (2026-31) focuses on the GIS-based Land Stack.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure chronological pair and then match the remaining phases by their distinctive focus.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the reported progress in land-record modernisation?
o: RoR digitised: 99.8%; SROs computerised: 95.73%; cadastral maps digitised: 97.24%
RoR digitised: 97.24%; SROs computerised: 99.8%; cadastral maps digitised: 95.73%
RoR digitised: 95.73%; SROs computerised: 99.8%; cadastral maps digitised: 97.24%
RoR digitised: 99.8%; SROs computerised: 97.24%; cadastral maps digitised: 95.73%
accepted.x: The reported figures are 99.8% for digitised Records of Rights, 95.73% for computerised Sub-Registrar Offices, and 97.24% for digitised cadastral maps.
accepted.tq: Split the three percentages by associating each figure with its specific indicator.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: NAKSHA, the urban pilot under DILRMP, is associated with which of the following?
o: NCAER, 168 districts, ₹194 crore and issuance of Bhoomi Samman certificates
Department of Land Resources, 29 States/UTs, ₹566.23 crore and issuance of ULPIN
Survey of India, more than 150 cities, ₹194 crore and issuance of ‘Ur Pro Card’
NICSI, 6.62 lakh villages, ₹566.23 crore and issuance of property cards
accepted.x: NAKSHA is an urban pilot under DILRMP implemented through the Survey of India. It covers more than 150 cities, has an allocation of ₹194 crore and issues the ‘Ur Pro Card’.
accepted.tq: Use the implementing agency, scale, cost and output as a four-part identification test.
accepted.sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

accepted.s: SVAMITVA stands for:
o: Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas
Systematic Valuation and Mapping of Inhabited Technology Villages and Areas
Survey of Village Assets and Mapping through Integrated Technology in Village Areas
State Verification and Mapping of Titles in Village Agricultural Areas
accepted.x: SVAMITVA expands to Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym, where similar words are the main distractors.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s: SVAMITVA was launched on which occasion and date?
o: National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2020
Constitution Day, 26 November 2020
Independence Day, 15 August 2021
National Panchayati Raj Day, 2 October 2020
accepted.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, the occasion of National Panchayati Raj Day. Its pilot was conducted in 2020 and it was taken nationwide in 2021.
accepted.tq: Combine the launch occasion with the exact date and distinguish it from the later nationwide rollout.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s: Which organisation is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA and which organisation provides its technology support?
o: NCAER and Department of Land Resources, respectively
Department of Land Resources and State Election Commissions, respectively
Survey of India and NICSI, respectively
NICSI and Survey of India, respectively
accepted.x: The Survey of India is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA, while NICSI provides technology support.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the implementing agency and the technology-support agency.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s:
With reference to the coverage and output of SVAMITVA, consider the following statements:
1. It covers rural inhabited or abadi areas.
2. Agricultural land is covered under the scheme’s property-card survey.
3. Property Cards function as Records of Rights and can be accessed through DigiLocker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: SVAMITVA covers rural inhabited or abadi areas, not agricultural land. Its output is Property Cards functioning as Records of Rights, with DigiLocker access.
accepted.tq: Watch for the scope trap involving inhabited village areas versus agricultural land.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the pilot States of SVAMITVA?
o: Haryana
Andhra Pradesh
Gujarat
Rajasthan
accepted.x: The pilot States included Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh. Gujarat was not included in the listed pilot States.
accepted.tq: Identify the omitted State by recalling the complete pilot-State list.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s: Which technology is used by SVAMITVA for geo-referencing, and who prepares and distributes the Property Cards?
o: NGDRS; NICSI alone
ULPIN; Survey of India alone
GIS Land Stack; Central Government alone
CORS; State governments
accepted.x: SVAMITVA uses Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) for geo-referencing. State governments prepare and distribute the Property Cards.
accepted.tq: Separate the geo-referencing technology from the authority responsible for card delivery.
accepted.sec: SVAMITVA - launch, ministry, drone survey, property cards, States

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the scale and extension of SVAMITVA:
1. The target is 6.62 lakh villages.
2. The cost is ₹566.23 crore.
3. The scheme has been extended up to 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only

accepted.s: As of December 2025, which of the following correctly states the progress of drone surveys under SVAMITVA?
o: 3.44 lakh villages surveyed against approximately 3.28 lakh notified villages
2.76 lakh villages surveyed against approximately 3.28 lakh notified villages
6.62 lakh villages surveyed against approximately 3.44 lakh notified villages
3.28 lakh villages surveyed against approximately 3.44 lakh notified villages
accepted.x: By December 2025, drone surveys had been completed in 3.28 lakh villages against approximately 3.44 lakh notified villages.
accepted.tq: Compare the completed figure with the notified target rather than reversing the two numbers.

accepted.s: The number of property cards generated under SVAMITVA was reported as:
o: 2.76 crore plus
6.62 crore plus
3.28 crore plus
2.42 crore plus

accepted.s: ULPIN, also known as Bhu-Aadhaar, refers to:
o: A 16-digit code issued only for agricultural loans
A 14-digit registration number based on the village population
A 12-digit numeric code based on the owner’s Aadhaar number
A 14-digit alphanumeric identification number generated from the geo-coordinates of a parcel’s vertices
accepted.x: ULPIN means Unique Land Parcel Identification Number, or Bhu-Aadhaar. It is a 14-digit alphanumeric ID derived from the geo-coordinates of a parcel’s vertices.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the parcel-based geo-coordinate identifier from personal Aadhaar and registration numbers.
accepted.sec: ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar - meaning, digits

accepted.s: The standards associated with ULPIN are:
o: ISO and WTO
ECCMA and OGC
NCAER and NGDRS
CORS and NICSI
accepted.x: ULPIN is based on the standards of ECCMA and OGC.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional-standard pair rather than the agencies connected with other land-record schemes.
accepted.sec: ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar - meaning, digits

accepted.s: According to the reported implementation status, ULPIN covered:
o: 16 States and 168 districts
18 States/UTs and 12 crore parcels
9 States and 6.62 lakh parcels
29 States/UTs and 36.67 crore parcels
accepted.x: ULPIN had been rolled out in 29 States/UTs and covered 36.67 crore parcels.
accepted.tq: Match the geographic coverage figure with the parcel-count figure.
accepted.sec: ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar - meaning, digits

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the presumptive and conclusive systems of land titling?
o: Under the presumptive system the State guarantees title, whereas under the conclusive system title may be challenged through earlier deeds.
Under the presumptive system registration records a transaction, whereas under the conclusive system the State guarantees the title once issued.
Both systems rely on separate registration, survey and revenue records with no authoritative title register.
Neither system permits disputes regarding title after mutation is recorded.
accepted.x: In the presumptive system, registration records a transaction and title may be challenged through earlier deeds, mutation or possession. In the conclusive system, the State guarantees the title once it is issued.
accepted.tq: Reverse the two systems mentally and compare who bears the guarantee and whether title remains challengeable.
accepted.sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

accepted.s: Which institutional arrangement characterises the conclusive land-titling system?
o: Registration, survey and revenue records are maintained separately.
A single authoritative title register is maintained.
Title is determined exclusively by possession records.
Only mutation records are maintained without registration records.
accepted.x: The conclusive system provides for a single authoritative title register, unlike the separate records maintained under the presumptive system.
accepted.tq: Use the record-structure distinction to separate the two titling models.
accepted.sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog Model Conclusive Land Titling Act, 2020:
1. It is a model framework.
2. Its adoption by States is compulsory.
3. It seeks to reduce disputes, facilitate credit and lower transaction costs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Act is a model framework and its objectives include fewer disputes, easier credit and lower transaction costs. Adoption is a matter of State choice, not compulsory.
accepted.tq: Spot the compulsory-adoption trap in an otherwise correct description of the model Act.
accepted.sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

accepted.s: The Supreme Court decision of 1 January 2026 concerning registration and title held that:
o: A transfer deed cannot be registered unless a nationwide survey has been completed.
Registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title, and mandatory proof of mutation under the Bihar rule was not upheld.
Mutation is always superior to a registered transfer deed.
Registration of a transfer deed by itself conclusively establishes title in every case.
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held that registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title and did not uphold the Bihar requirement of mandatory proof of mutation. The judgment noted that land had not been surveyed nationwide since 1950.
accepted.tq: Focus on the legal distinction between registration, mutation and title rather than treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

accepted.s: NGDRS is best described as:
o: A common, configurable registration application for sub-registrars and citizens under DILRMP
A drone-based village-survey platform operated exclusively by Survey of India
A ranking system for assessing the quality of State land records
A land-dispute tribunal established under the Model Conclusive Land Titling Act
accepted.x: The National Generic Document Registration System is the ‘One Nation One Registration Software’ under DILRMP, serving sub-registrars and citizens through a common configurable application.
accepted.tq: Identify the function of NGDRS and distinguish software, survey, adjudication and ranking institutions.
accepted.sec: National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported adoption and data-sharing status of NGDRS?
o: Adopted by 29 States/UTs and shared by 16 more
Adopted by 16 States and shared by 168 districts
Adopted by 18 States/UTs and shared by 12 more
Adopted by 12 States/UTs and shared by 18 more
accepted.x: NGDRS had been adopted by 18 States/UTs, while 12 more States/UTs shared data through the system.
accepted.tq: Keep adoption and data-sharing counts in their correct order.
accepted.sec: National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS)

accepted.s: The NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI) evaluates States primarily on:
o: Agricultural output and irrigation coverage
Village population and drone-survey expenditure
Industrial investment and export performance
Digitisation and quality of land records
accepted.x: NCAER’s Land Records and Services Index grades States on the digitisation and quality of their land records.
accepted.tq: Match the index with the specific dimensions it measures, not with broader economic indicators.
accepted.sec: Land Records Index (NCAER N-LRSI) - AP rank

accepted.s: The ‘Bhoomi Samman’ Platinum grade was awarded by the Department of Land Resources to:
o: 16 districts in 168 States
29 States/UTs covering 36.67 crore parcels
168 districts in 16 States
150 cities in 16 States
accepted.x: The Department of Land Resources awarded the Bhoomi Samman Platinum grade to 168 districts in 16 States.
accepted.tq: Separate the number of districts from the number of States in the award statistic.
